title: Coin-tape conversion preserves complexity
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$ with input sets $X$, $Y$ and output type $\alpha$. For every real number $\delta > 0$, the coin-tape conversion of $p$ at slack $\delta$ yields a length $n$ and a finite-message protocol over $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ whose communication complexity equals the communication complexity of $p$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite probability space
p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω with inputs X, Y and output α
replaced:
For any finite-message protocol $p$ over a finite probability space $\Omega$ and any
$\delta > 0$, the complexity of the \texttt{CoinTape} approximation
$(p.\mathrm{toCoinTape}\;\delta).2$ equals the complexity of the original protocol $p$.
